tips.title: Write the deposit, its refund date and the permitted deductions into the lease — no statute will do it for you
tips.cost: No monetary cost. It takes ten extra minutes at signing. The challenge is raising it in front of the landlord.
tips.inPlainWords: Indian tenancy law is state law — the Model Tenancy Act, 2021 in the states that adopted it, and older rent control Acts elsewhere — so there is no national rule that dictates what a deposit clause must say. What you can do is put three things in writing: how much the deposit is, when it comes back, and what it can be deducted for. Those three lines are what a court or a rent authority will read when the landlord keeps the money.
tips.benefit: The Model Tenancy Act, 2021, which states may adopt, limits the security deposit for residential premises to two months' rent and requires it to be refunded when the tenant hands back possession, after deducting arrears and the cost of damage beyond normal wear. Where your state has not adopted the Act, the deposit is whatever the lease says, which is exactly why the lease should say it. A clause that names the amount, the refund date and the deductions can be enforced; a bare “deposit adjustable” cannot. A deduction for “cleaning” or “repainting” that the lease does not mention is hard to defend.
tips.sources: Model Tenancy Act, 2021. <https://mohua.gov.in/>; National Legal Services Authority. <https://nalsa.gov.in/>; Transfer of Property Act, 1882. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>
tips.caveats: On the day you move out, take photos and videos with the landlord present and record the water, electricity and gas meter readings. If the deposit is withheld without cause, send a written demand; in a state with a Rent Authority under the Model Tenancy Act, complain there, and elsewhere use the civil court or free legal aid through the District Legal Services Authority (NALSA, 15100). For a small amount, a legal notice is often enough.

tips.title: If the water or power is cut, the locks are changed or you are threatened with being thrown out, call 112 and record everything — self-help eviction is not a lawful remedy
tips.cost: No cost. One call to 112 and a written complaint at the police station; keep copies of both.
tips.inPlainWords: A landlord who wants you out has to use the law: a notice to quit under the lease or the state rent Act, and then an order from a court or the Rent Authority. Cutting the water or power, changing the locks, removing your belongings or threatening you is not a shortcut that the law recognises. Call 112 if you are being threatened or kept out of the house, and keep the police complaint, because it is the record you will need later. Do not confront the landlord alone.
tips.benefit: India has no single national statute that says “a landlord may not cut the utilities”; tenancy is state law. Where a state has adopted the Model Tenancy Act, 2021, the landlord must give notice and obtain an order before taking back possession, and a tenant facing an illegal eviction can apply to the Rent Authority. Elsewhere the route is the state rent Act and the civil court. Separately, locking a tenant out, throwing out their belongings or holding them off by threat can amount to criminal trespass, mischief and wrongful restraint under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, which is why the police complaint matters even while the tenancy dispute is civil.
tips.sources: Model Tenancy Act, 2021. <https://mohua.gov.in/>; Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; National Legal Services Authority. <https://nalsa.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: Calling 112 gives you an official record of the date and time; the police may treat the dispute as civil, but the complaint still exists. Photograph the changed lock, the disconnected meter and the removed belongings, and keep the lease, the rent receipts and the bank statements. Tell the Rent Authority where one exists, and the municipal water or electricity authority if the supply itself was cut.

tips.title: Agents are not a party to your lease: pay the landlord, or an agent the landlord has authorised in writing
tips.cost: No cost. A few minutes to check the name on the lease and the bank account before you pay.
tips.inPlainWords: India has no rule that forbids a broker from collecting rent; plenty of landlords authorise an agent to do exactly that. What matters is authority. The person you pay should be the landlord named in the lease, or someone the landlord has authorised in writing. Money paid to someone without authority can be treated as rent unpaid, and you can face eviction for arrears even though you paid. Check the name against the lease and the sale deed, ask for a written authorisation, and pay by bank transfer.
tips.benefit: Nothing in Indian law stops an agent from receiving rent or a deposit on the landlord's behalf, so a blanket rule against it would be wrong. The protection comes from evidence: a lease naming the landlord and the payee, a signed authorisation where the money goes to a relative or an agency, and a bank transfer with a receipt in the landlord's name. Where a broker collects, insist on a receipt that names the landlord and the period the rent covers. A broker's commission for finding the property is a separate fee and is not rent.
tips.sources: Model Tenancy Act, 2021. <https://mohua.gov.in/>; Transfer of Property Act, 1882. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; National Legal Services Authority. <https://nalsa.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: If the payee is not the landlord, ask for a written authorisation signed by the landlord; a chat message from an unknown number is not enough. Match the name to the sale deed where you can. Keep every receipt, because it is the only proof that the rent was paid.

tips.title: Before you pay a year's rent upfront to a rental company, ask who is holding the money — India has no rental escrow account to protect you
tips.cost: No cost to ask. A title check and a lawyer's letter cost a little; losing a year's rent costs a lot.
tips.inPlainWords: In India there is no statutory escrow account for a residential rental business, so a company that collects a year's rent in advance is holding your money as an ordinary debtor. If it stops paying the landlord or closes down, you lose the prepaid rent and the deposit, and you may still owe the lender if you borrowed to pay it. Pay month to month where you can; if you do pay in advance, get a written receipt, pay by bank transfer, and check the company's registration and the landlord's ownership.
tips.benefit: India has no equivalent of a supervised rental escrow account, so the protection has to come from the contract itself and from the ordinary law of cheating: a written agreement naming the landlord, the rent, the deposit and the refund terms; payment by bank transfer to an account in the landlord's or the company's name; and, if the company takes deposits from many tenants and then disappears, a criminal complaint for cheating and criminal breach of trust under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, plus a civil suit for recovery. The RBI's prepaid-instrument rules cover wallets and vouchers, not a landlord's rent.
tips.sources: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs. <https://mohua.gov.in/>; Reserve Bank of India. <https://www.rbi.org.in/>; Ministry of Corporate Affairs, company search. <https://www.mca.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: Ask for the landlord's name on the sale deed, the company's CIN and registered address, and the clause that says who refunds the deposit and when. If a “rent loan” is part of the deal, read the loan agreement: the lender's claim is against you, not the rental company. Avoid any arrangement where you pay a year upfront and repay a lender monthly.

tips.title: House sold during your lease: the lease does not end with the sale, and a registered lease is what protects you
tips.cost: No cost beyond the stamp duty and registration fee the state charges for a lease of a year or more.
tips.inPlainWords: If the house is sold while you are still renting it, your lease does not automatically end: the buyer takes the property subject to a lease they knew about, which is why a written lease matters and a registered one matters more. An unregistered lease of a year or more is hard to prove and easier for a buyer to ignore. Keep the lease, the rent receipts and proof of the date you moved in.
tips.benefit: A lease is a transfer of an interest in immovable property under section 105 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, so a sale of the house does not by itself determine the lease; the purchaser steps into the lessor's shoes and is bound by a lease of which they had notice. Section 17(1)(d) of the Registration Act, 1908 requires a lease for a term exceeding one year, or reserving a yearly rent, to be registered, and section 49 makes an unregistered lease inadmissible as evidence of the lease. Where a state has adopted the Model Tenancy Act, 2021, the tenancy agreement must be registered with the Rent Authority.
tips.sources: Transfer of Property Act, 1882 (section 105; section 106, notice to quit). <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Registration Act, 1908 (section 17(1)(d)). <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Model Tenancy Act, 2021. <https://mohua.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: This applies only if you are lawfully in possession; keep the lease, the rent receipts and proof of the move-in date. If a buyer asks you to leave before the term ends, do not hand over possession on a phone call: ask for a written notice under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act or the state rent Act, and get advice from the District Legal Services Authority (NALSA, 15100) if you need it.

tips.title: Check who actually owns the flat, and whether it is mortgaged, before you sign anything — and make every payment by bank transfer with a purpose note
tips.cost: No cost involved. The check takes about half an hour.
tips.inPlainWords: The two common ways people lose money at the start of a tenancy are paying rent to someone who is not the owner, and taking a flat that is already mortgaged and later enforced against. Before you sign, ask for the sale deed or title deed, and check the encumbrance certificate for the property with the sub-registrar where the deed is registered — most states now issue it online through their registration portal. Confirm that the person you are paying is the owner named in the deed. If a relative or an agent signs instead, get a written authority and check it against the deed. Make every payment by bank transfer with a note such as “rent for [address], [month]”, and keep the receipt: the bank record is the evidence that survives a dispute.
tips.benefit: Paying a person who does not own the flat, or taking a flat that is already charged to a lender, accounts for most of the money lost at the start of a tenancy. The sale deed and the encumbrance certificate tell you who owns the property and what is charged against it, and a bank transfer with a purpose note proves what you paid and for what. That record is what you produce before the Rent Authority where the state has adopted the Model Tenancy Act, 2021, before a civil court, or in a police complaint if the money was taken by deception.
tips.sources: Registration Act, 1908 (section 17, documents of which registration is compulsory). <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Transfer of Property Act, 1882 (sections 54 and 55, sale and the duties of buyer and seller). <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; National Legal Services Authority, free legal aid. <https://nalsa.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: The title and encumbrance records sit with the sub-registrar’s office where the deed was registered, and a search of the registered documents is open to anyone on payment of the prescribed fee. At signing, the owner named in the deed should be present; if not, insist on a written authority and check it against the deed. If you are renting from a tenant, check that the lease allows subletting and get the owner’s written consent — a sub-lease without consent can be terminated. Where the flat is in a co-operative society, ask for the society’s no-objection certificate and its share certificate.

tips.title: For a second-hand home, route the payment through a bank and do not hand cash to the agent
tips.cost: Stamp duty and registration fees are the main cost. A lawyer's title check is worth the fee.
tips.inPlainWords: India does not require an escrow for a resale flat, but a large cash payment to an agent is how buyers lose money. Pay by bank transfer to the seller's account, make the payment against the registered sale deed, and keep the bank record. For a new project, the RERA Act, 2016 requires the developer to keep 70% of the project receipts in a separate escrow account.
tips.benefit: The Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016 requires a developer to deposit 70% of the amounts realised from buyers in a separate project account, and the state RERA authority can act on a violation. A resale transaction is governed by the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 and the Registration Act, 1908; the sale deed must be registered. A bank transfer and a receipt are evidence of payment. A cash payment without a receipt is hard to prove.
tips.sources: Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Transfer of Property Act, 1882. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Registration Act, 1908. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Reserve Bank of India. <https://www.rbi.org.in/>
tips.caveats: An agent's 'token' is not a legal title. Do not pay before the title search and the encumbrance certificate. A power of attorney sale needs a registered power of attorney.

tips.title: Don’t rent a subdivided flat on trust: India has no national rule on the smallest rentable unit, so check the sanctioned plan, the municipal bye-laws and the lease
tips.cost: There’s no direct expense. The trade-off is that on the same budget you will have to live farther out or in a smaller space.
tips.inPlainWords: India has no national rule fixing the smallest rentable unit. What decides whether a flat may be divided, and which rooms may be slept in, is the local municipal building bye-laws, the sanctioned plan for that building, the fire-safety rules and your lease. A room built after sanction, or a flat split into more units than the plan allows, is unauthorised construction, and the municipality can act against it. Ask to see the sanctioned plan, the lease and, in a co-operative society, the society’s no-objection certificate before you pay.
tips.benefit: No Union law says a kitchen, a bathroom or a balcony can never be lived in, and there is no national minimum floor area per tenant. The limits come from local law. Municipal and state building bye-laws set minimum room sizes, ventilation and occupancy; the sanctioned plan shows what the building was approved to contain; the state fire rules and the National Building Code of India, 2016 govern exits and means of escape; and the lease says what you have rented and on what terms. A landlord who subdivides without sanction is exposed to the municipality, and you are exposed with him: the unit can be sealed or pulled down and you can be asked to leave. On rent, no rule stops a landlord from raising it at the end of the term, but during the term the rent clause in your agreement binds him, and in a state that has adopted the Model Tenancy Act, 2021 the tenancy law governs notice and eviction.
tips.sources: Bureau of Indian Standards, National Building Code of India, 2016 (Part 4: fire and life safety). <https://www.bis.gov.in/>; Delhi Building Bye-Laws, 2016, an example of the state and municipal bye-laws that fix room sizes and occupancy — the bye-laws of your own city apply. <https://delhi.gov.in/>; National Legal Services Authority, free legal aid. <https://nalsa.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: When an unauthorised subdivision is taken up by the municipality, tenants bear the cost of moving out and often cannot recover the security deposit or the prepaid rent. Safety matters more than the rent: makeshift walls block emergency exits, and overcrowding a single flat overloads the wiring. At the viewing, check three things — whether walls were added after the plan was sanctioned, whether the room has a window that opens to the outside, and whether the electrical connection and meter can carry the number of people who will live there. Get the list of what is let, the fixtures and the meter reading written into the lease, and keep a dated video of the flat as it was handed over.

tips.title: India has no household-register bar on rural housing, but land-purchase rules depend on the state
tips.cost: A lawyer and a revenue-record check cost money; a bad purchase costs more.
tips.inPlainWords: India has no household-registration system that stops an urban resident from renting a rural house. Buying agricultural land, however, is restricted in many states: a non-agriculturist may need permission, and some states bar outsiders altogether. A long lease or a rent agreement is the safer route. Check the state land-revenue law before you pay.
tips.benefit: Land is a state subject. Many states restrict the purchase of agricultural land by a non-agriculturist, and some require the buyer to be a resident. The Registration Act, 1908 requires a sale deed for immovable property to be registered, and the state stamp duty applies. A lease for more than a year should be registered. A village house on non-agricultural land may be bought, but the title and the land-use classification must be checked.
tips.sources: Registration Act, 1908. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Transfer of Property Act, 1882. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Ministry of Rural Development. <https://rural.nic.in/>
tips.caveats: A 'farmhouse' on agricultural land may not be a lawful residential plot. A power-of-attorney transfer is not a substitute for a registered sale deed. Check the encumbrance certificate and the mutation record.

tips.title: Buying under construction? Check the RERA registration first, and pay only into the project account it names
tips.cost: No financial outlay. A few minutes on the state RERA portal before you pay.
tips.inPlainWords: An under-construction project can only be advertised, booked or sold after it is registered with the state RERA, and the registration number must appear in the advertisement and the agreement. The developer must keep 70% of the money collected from buyers in a separate project account in a scheduled bank, to be used for that project's land and construction, and may withdraw it only in proportion to the work certified by an engineer, an architect and a chartered accountant. Pay only into the account named in the agreement, and check the project's quarterly progress reports on the RERA portal.
tips.benefit: Section 3 of the Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016 bars a promoter from advertising, marketing, booking or selling a plot, apartment or building without registering the project with the state RERA. Section 4(2)(l)(D) requires 70% of the amounts realised from allottees to be deposited in a separate account in a scheduled bank and withdrawn only after certification by an engineer, an architect and a chartered accountant. Section 11 lists the promoter's duties, including quarterly updates on the RERA website, and section 19 gives the allottee the right to the sanctioned plans and the stage-wise schedule. Section 18 gives the remedy when possession is delayed.
tips.sources: Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs. <https://mohua.gov.in/>; Reserve Bank of India. <https://www.rbi.org.in/>
tips.caveats: The state RERA portal is the only reliable check: the registration number, the project account, the quarterly updates and the complaints against the promoter. Money paid before registration is not protected by the Act, so do not pay a “pre-launch” token on a verbal promise. If the developer defaults, the complaint goes to the state RERA authority.

tips.title: If the deal fails for a reason that is nobody's fault, ask for the booking amount back in writing — India gives you no automatic refund, so put the term in the agreement
tips.cost: No monetary cost to ask. A written demand is free; a consumer complaint or a civil suit is not.
tips.inPlainWords: There is no Indian statute that gives a homebuyer an automatic refund of a booking deposit when the sale falls through. What you have is contract: the booking form and the agreement for sale decide whether the amount is refundable, forfeitable or adjustable, and whether a refused home loan counts as your fault. Before you pay anything, make the trigger explicit — if the loan is not sanctioned on these terms, the booking amount is refunded in full within a stated number of days — and pay by bank transfer with a receipt.
tips.benefit: Indian law treats the booking amount as a contractual deposit, not a statutory one. If the seller backs out or cannot complete the sale, the buyer can sue for the return of the money and, where the seller's breach is established, for damages; if the buyer walks away without justification, the seller may forfeit a reasonable part of the deposit, and a court will not enforce a penalty out of proportion to the loss. For a RERA-registered project, the allottee's remedy for delay or failure to deliver is in section 18 of the RERA Act, which provides interest or a refund with interest. For a resale, the refund and specific-performance routes are contractual.
tips.sources: Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Department of Consumer Affairs. <https://consumeraffairs.nic.in/>; National Legal Services Authority. <https://nalsa.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: Put the refund trigger and the loan contingency in the agreement, not in a chat message. Read the forfeiture clause, because many booking forms forfeit the whole amount if the buyer does not sign within a fixed number of days. If a refund is refused, send a written demand, then use the consumer commission for a deficiency in service or a civil suit; a RERA-registered project can also be complained about to the state RERA.

tips.title: Get the carpet area and the refund clause into the agreement before you sign, and keep the brochure and the sales-hall photographs
tips.cost: Zero financial outlay. Read the area clause before you sign, and keep the brochure, the price sheet and dated photographs of the model flat.
tips.inPlainWords: India has no statutory area-error formula. What you have is the agreement: the RERA Act requires the carpet area of the apartment to be disclosed and stated in the agreement for sale of a registered project, and the builder must deliver what the agreement promises. If the flat is materially smaller than the agreed carpet area, the claim is for a proportionate refund and, in a registered project, a complaint to the state RERA. The brochure and the show-flat photographs matter because a false or misleading description of what is being sold is an unfair trade practice under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.
tips.benefit: For a RERA-registered project, the promoter must disclose the carpet area and the agreement for sale must state it; delivering materially less than that is a breach, and the allottee can complain to the state RERA under section 31 and claim the proportionate refund. Section 14 requires the promoter to complete the project in accordance with the sanctioned plans. Under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, a false or misleading description of a product or service is an unfair trade practice, and a misleading advertisement can also be taken to the Central Consumer Protection Authority. The brochure, the price sheet and dated photographs of the model flat are the evidence of what was offered.
tips.sources: Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016 (sections 14 and 31). <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Consumer Protection Act, 2019. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Department of Consumer Affairs. <https://consumeraffairs.nic.in/>; Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs. <https://mohua.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: Read the definition of area in the agreement: builders often quote “super built-up area”, which includes a share of common areas and is larger than the carpet area you actually get, so compare like with like. A clause allowing the builder to vary the area by a percentage is common, so check what happens to the price if it does. Keep the original brochure and dated photographs of the model flat. Delay in delivery is covered in Chapter 15, item 13; handover defects in item 18.

tips.title: If the builder is late handing over or late with the registry, send a written demand and then use section 18 of the RERA Act
tips.cost: Zero monetary cost for the demand. A RERA complaint or a civil suit costs time and, for a lawyer, money.
tips.inPlainWords: If possession is late, the RERA Act gives you a choice: interest on the amount you paid for every month of delay, or withdrawal with a refund of the amount paid plus interest. Send a written demand first, by email to the address in the agreement and by registered post, because the date of the demand is what you will point to later. If the project is not RERA-registered, the RERA route is closed and the claim is contractual, in the consumer commission or a civil court.
tips.benefit: Section 18 of the Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016 provides that if the promoter fails to complete or is unable to give possession in accordance with the agreement, the promoter is liable on demand to return the amount received with interest, and to pay interest for every month of delay until possession; the allottee may withdraw from the project. The rate of interest is set by the rules of the state where the project is registered. For delay in executing the conveyance deed, the promoter's duty is in section 17, and the complaint goes to the state RERA under section 31. Where the agreement itself fixes a penalty or interest, that clause applies, subject to the statutory floor.
tips.sources: Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016 (sections 17, 18, 31). <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs. <https://mohua.gov.in/>; National Legal Services Authority. <https://nalsa.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: Do not accept a “grace period” letter as a substitute for possession. Keep every payment receipt, the allotment letter and the agreement, because the amount you paid is what the interest is computed on. A RERA complaint should be filed early; authorities can condone delay, but a long wait weakens the case. If the builder offers a settlement, check whether it covers the interest you are entitled to before you sign.

tips.title: Search the title for mortgages and court attachments before you pay, and register the sale deed after you sign — India has no provisional registration
tips.cost: A few dozen rupees for an encumbrance certificate and the registration fee for the deed. Half a day at the sub-registrar's office.
tips.inPlainWords: For a resale flat or a plot, the check happens in the seller's documents and at the sub-registrar's office: the sale deeds going back, the encumbrance certificate for the period you care about, the property tax receipts, the society's no-dues certificate for a flat, and any mortgage or court attachment. In most states the encumbrance certificate can be applied for online through the registration department's portal. After you sign, the sale deed must be stamped and registered; until it is registered, you do not have a title you can enforce against a later buyer.
tips.benefit: India has no provisional or advance-notice registration. The protection comes from two statutes. Section 17 of the Registration Act, 1908 makes registration compulsory for a sale deed of immovable property, and section 49 makes an unregistered document inadmissible to prove the transfer. Under section 54 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 a sale of tangible immovable property of the value of one hundred rupees and upwards is made only by a registered instrument, and title passes on registration, not on payment. Section 50 of the Registration Act gives a registered document effect against an unregistered one, which is why a later buyer who registers promptly can defeat an earlier buyer who did not.
tips.sources: Registration Act, 1908 (sections 17, 49, 50). <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Transfer of Property Act, 1882 (section 54). <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs. <https://mohua.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: An encumbrance certificate covers only registered transactions in that sub-registrar's jurisdiction, so a mortgage registered elsewhere will not appear; ask the seller for the lender's no-objection certificate and check the society's records for a flat. Pay the stamp duty and registration fee in the state's prescribed manner, keep the registered deed and the receipt, and check mutation of the revenue records where the property is a plot or agricultural land. Verifying the seller's identity and the title chain before signing is covered in Chapter 15, Rule 6.

tips.title: If new home loans are cheaper than yours, ask your lender to reset the rate — or refinance the balance with another lender
tips.cost: No cost to ask. Switching a loan to another lender may carry a processing fee; prepayment of a floating-rate home loan is free of charge under the RBI's rules.
tips.inPlainWords: A floating-rate loan does not automatically follow the market when it falls. Under the RBI's rules a floating-rate retail loan must be linked to an external benchmark, and the spread over that benchmark is fixed for the life of the loan; the rate is reset at stated intervals, so ask when your next reset is due. If new borrowers are being offered a lower spread, ask your lender to reduce it or refinance the balance with a lender that will. Compare the effective annualised rate, not the advertised one, and ask for the reset clause in writing.
tips.benefit: The RBI's circular on interest rate reset of floating-rate loans required new retail and MSME loans to be linked to an external benchmark such as the policy repo rate, with the spread fixed for the life of the loan and the rate reset at stated intervals. A later RBI direction on the reset of floating-rate loans required lenders to communicate a reset clearly and not to raise the spread arbitrarily. RBI rules also bar foreclosure charges on a floating-rate home loan, which is what makes switching or part-prepaying practical. If your loan predates these rules, the loan agreement decides, so read the reset clause before you ask.
tips.sources: Reserve Bank of India, interest rate reset of floating-rate loans. <https://www.rbi.org.in/>; Reserve Bank of India, integrated ombudsman scheme. <https://www.rbi.org.in/>; National Housing Bank. <https://nhb.org.in/>
tips.caveats: Ask what the effective annualised rate is and compare it with what a new borrower is offered today. A switch costs something: processing fee, legal and valuation charges, and paperwork. A part-prepayment cuts the balance and the interest, but check whether it shortens the tenure or reduces the EMI, and decide which you want. If the lender refuses to reset, complain first to the lender's grievance officer, then to the RBI Ombudsman under the Reserve Bank's integrated ombudsman scheme.

tips.title: For a first home, compare a bank home loan, an EPF housing advance and the PMAY-U 2.0 interest subsidy before you sign
tips.cost: Nothing is charged for comparing the options. The extra work is time: the EPF advance is applied for through the employer and the EPFO, and it is sanctioned only for a house purchase or construction and subject to the service conditions in the EPF Scheme, 1952; a bank or housing-finance company loan needs the sale deed, the encumbrance certificate and proof of income, and sanction takes longer than a plain enquiry. Read the loan agreement before you sign it and do not sign a blank one.
tips.inPlainWords: India has no single “provident fund plus commercial” mortgage product. The routes are a bank or housing-finance company loan, an advance from your EPF account for a house purchase or construction, and the interest subsidy under Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana — Urban 2.0 for an eligible household. Compare the interest rate, the processing fee, the loan-to-value and the prepayment terms. Ask which PMAY version the lender is actually claiming for you: the earlier credit-linked subsidy scheme under PMAY-U closed on 31 March 2021, and PMAY-U 2.0, approved in 2024, is the scheme now on offer. Do not sign a blank loan agreement.
tips.benefit: The EPF Scheme, 1952 allows a member to take an advance for a house purchase or construction, subject to the service and cost conditions. PMAY-U 2.0 gives an interest subsidy on home loans for eligible EWS, LIG and MIG households through participating lenders, within income and carpet-area limits; the older credit-linked subsidy window closed on 31 March 2021. A bank loan is governed by the RBI’s fair-practice code, and the loan agreement must state the rate, the fees and the prepayment terms. Before any of that, the title and the encumbrance certificate are required.
tips.sources: Reserve Bank of India, home loans and fair practice. <https://www.rbi.org.in/>; National Housing Bank. <https://nhb.org.in/>; Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation. <https://www.epfo.gov.in/>; Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana — Urban. <https://pmay-urban.gov.in/>; Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, PMAY-U. <https://pmaymis.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: A “teaser” rate can reset higher. A prepayment penalty may apply on a fixed-rate loan. The EPF advance reduces the retirement corpus. Check your PMAY-U 2.0 eligibility before you pay a booking amount, and do not rely on a builder’s brochure that still quotes the closed credit-linked subsidy.

tips.title: A society or property manager cannot cut your water or power to make you pay maintenance — the routes are the registrar, the utility regulator and the consumer commission
tips.cost: Zero financial outlay. A written complaint to the society and to the distribution company takes an hour; a consumer complaint has a small fee.
tips.inPlainWords: In a housing society or apartment association the managing committee can levy maintenance charges and can sue for arrears, but cutting off water, electricity, lift access or the gate to force payment is not a lawful collection method. Electricity comes from the distribution licensee, not the society; if the supply is being cut, complain to the distribution company and to the state electricity regulatory commission's consumer grievance forum. For a cooperative housing society, complain to the Registrar of Cooperative Societies. Keep paying what you actually owe, under protest and in writing, while you dispute the rest.
tips.benefit: The governing law is state law and the supply contract, not a national property-management regulation. A distribution licensee can disconnect supply only under the Electricity Act, 2003, and section 56 requires at least fifteen clear days' written notice before a disconnection for non-payment; a dispute between a member and a society is not a ground. Under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, a housing society or builder that provides a service for consideration is a service provider, so a deficiency can be taken to the District Consumer Commission. Where the society is a cooperative society, the Registrar of Cooperative Societies has powers over its management under the state cooperative societies Act; where the property is governed by an apartment ownership Act, that Act and the association's rules apply.
tips.sources: Electricity Act, 2003 (section 56). <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Consumer Protection Act, 2019. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Department of Consumer Affairs. <https://consumeraffairs.nic.in/>; Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs. <https://mohua.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: If your own electricity bill is unpaid, the distribution company can disconnect after notice, and that is lawful; it is separate from a society dispute. Photograph the disconnection, keep the receipts for what you have paid, and put the dispute in writing to the managing committee. If the water supply was cut, the municipal water authority is the second complaint route. Recovering money for spoiled food or damaged appliances needs a consumer complaint or a civil suit.

tips.title: On handover, inspect room by room and put every defect in writing — for five years the developer must fix structural defects and defects in workmanship
tips.cost: Zero financial cost. Two to three hours on handover day, room by room, with photographs of every defect. A professional inspection is optional and costs a fee.
tips.inPlainWords: For a RERA-registered project, the developer is liable for five years from the date of possession for a structural defect or a defect in workmanship, quality or provision of services, and must rectify it at its own cost within thirty days of a written notice. So inspect on the day you get the keys, list the cracks, damp patches, leaking taps, faulty wiring and ill-fitting doors in a written handover note or email, photograph them and keep a copy. If the developer does not fix them, complain to the state RERA.
tips.benefit: Section 14(3) of the Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016 makes the promoter liable to rectify a structural defect or any other defect in workmanship, quality or provision of services, at the promoter's cost, within thirty days of a written notice from the allottee, and the claim can be made within five years from the date of handing over possession. If the promoter fails to rectify within that period, the allottee is entitled to appropriate compensation under section 18. For a property outside RERA, the claim is contractual against the builder, or a consumer complaint for a deficiency in service under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.
tips.sources: Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016 (section 14). <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs. <https://mohua.gov.in/>; Department of Consumer Affairs. <https://consumeraffairs.nic.in/>
tips.caveats: The written handover note is what starts the thirty-day clock, so do not accept a verbal “we will fix it”. Do not begin major renovation before the defects are recorded, because the developer will blame your contractor. Keep the occupancy certificate, the completion certificate and the agreement. In a resale flat the builder's five-year obligation runs from the first possession, not from your purchase. Delay in delivery or in the conveyance deed is covered in Chapter 15, Rule 13.
